title: Chocolate Banana Icebox Cake
changes_from_base: A cooked vanilla custard lightened with whipped cream, layered with chocolate wafers and sliced bananas and set in the fridge, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: A classic custard-based icebox cake layers rich vanilla custard with chocolate wafer biscuits and sliced banana, finished with whipped cream and a dusting of cocoa.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 150 g caster sugar, 30 g cornflour and ¼ tsp fine salt in a pan, then gradually whisk in the 710 ml whole milk followed by the 6 egg yolks.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and at a low boil, 4-5 min, then whisk for 1 min more so the custard is well above 77 °C.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Push the custard through a sieve into a bowl, stir in 2 tsp vanilla, and cool to room temperature, about 1½ h.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Whip 175 ml of the double cream to stiff peaks and fold into the cooled custard.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spoon 120 ml custard into the serving dish, cover with about 15 chocolate wafers broken to fit, top with sliced banana from the 4 bananas, then spread over a third of the remaining custard.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Repeat the layers twice more, finishing with a layer of custard on top.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Whip the 355 ml double cream with 2 tbsp icing sugar to medium-stiff peaks, spread over the cake and sift cocoa powder over to finish.

tips: Cook the custard until it is well above a gentle boil so it sets properly once chilled.
Cool the custard fully before folding in the whipped cream to keep it light.
Chill for at least 4 h so the biscuits soften into a cake-like texture.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within the 24 h chilling window, as the bananas soften the longer it sits.
